title: PeaceOS Verifiable Evidence Package (VEP) manifest
description: Schema for manifest.json inside a .vep package. This file is the source of truth for the VEP format, version 0.1.
$comment: This schema fixes field SHAPE only. The exact bytes that get hashed, signed and timestamped (content, content_hash, signed_content) are defined in CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md, which this schema's package_id, signature and timestamps[].target fields reference.

package_id.description: Self-verifying identifier: "sha256:" + content_hash (see CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md). Excluded from `content`, so it is derived from content_hash rather than included in it — this field only pins the string SHAPE; Verify MUST additionally recompute content_hash and check equality.

created_at.description: When the manifest was assembled and signed.

custody.description: Chain-of-custody events (captured, imported, exported, ...). Part of the format from v0.1; signature and ordering are verified from M2 onward.

redactions.description: Withheld sensitive fields, represented only as salted commitments, never as plaintext. Part of the format from v0.1; commitment checks land in M2.

signature.description: Pseudonymous field signature over the manifest (protects the documenter's identity).

org.description: Organizational countersignature — the root of trust, anchored in the transparency directory.

withheld.description: true = this asset's bytes are deliberately not shipped in assets/ (asset-level redaction). Its sha256/size_bytes/media_type are still signed, so Verify reports it as "withheld but committed" rather than an integrity failure. Absent or false = the file MUST be present (M1 behavior, unchanged). See CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md §10.

captureClaim.description: Unverified metadata claimed by the capturing app/device. Never a source of trust by itself.

custodyEvent.description: Ed25519-signed over event_hash = SHA-256(JCS({event, actor, at})); see CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md §9.

actor.description: Pseudonymous actor key_id for this event (custody[0] is expected to be "captured"; not necessarily the same actor as the top-level field signature).

actor_public_key_ref.description: Path within the package to this event's actor's raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key file, e.g. "keys/coord-02.pub". Same pattern as signature.public_key_ref.

actor_public_key_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw public key bytes at actor_public_key_ref. Part of the custodyEvent object, which lives inside `content` — protected transitively via content_hash, the same way assets[].sha256 is, with no separate attestation chain needed (unlike the top-level signature.public_key_sha256, which protects the key that itself signs content).

commitment.description: SHA-256(JCS({ salt, field, value })), hex-encoded. The construction (why a JCS object instead of raw concatenation) lives in CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md. The salt is NEVER included in the package — the organization custodies it and reveals it only when disclosing the field.

target.description: The timestamp proof anchors content_hash = SHA-256(JCS(content)); see CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md.

fieldSignature.description: Pseudonymous field signature over content_hash. Signs a hash, not raw content, so the signing payload stays a fixed-size digest regardless of package size.

public_key_ref.description: Path within the package to the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key file, e.g. "keys/field-01.pub". Lets Verify check the field signature fully offline.

public_key_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw public key bytes at public_key_ref. Part of `signature`, therefore covered by the org countersignature (see CRYPTO_CONTRACT.md) — this is how the org vouches for the field key without the key traveling outside the signed envelope.

transparency_ref.description: Pointer into the public transparency repo, e.g. "git:keys@<commit-hash>".
